governingDocuments.AGENTS.md: Repository owner standing branch and agent policy. The owner's current explicit instruction supersedes stale additive-only test cadence wording where necessary for the governed Orchestrator architecture.
governingDocuments.DEVLOG.md: Repository-visible chain of custody and current shared AI handoff.
governingDocuments.AI-CONFLICTS.json: Auditable AI conflict ledger; never bypass or disable it.
governingDocuments.src/handoffPolicy.js: Enforces takeover-ready handoff and DEVLOG chain of custody through validateHandoffPlan and validateDevlogChainOfCustody, including the bounded Command log archive requirements.
governingDocuments.src/testCadence.js: The governed Orchestrator entry point. It preserves natural-language selection authority, applies run governance, and exposes owner-defined category cadence plus a test-only every-push baseline.
governingDocuments.src/testCadenceCore.js: Active Orchestrator cadence layer. It delegates mature selection behavior to the preserved legacy core while owning category cadence: Code every push, Security daily, Utility twice weekly, Maintenance weekly.
governingDocuments.src/testCadenceCoreLegacy.js: Byte-for-byte preserved prior Orchestrator selection core used underneath the active cadence layer so mature request interpretation and change-impact selection remain intact.
governingDocuments.src/testRunGovernance.js: Orchestrator run governance for 60-second test progress updates, category-derived criticality, known-bug persistence, severity ordering, and mandatory passing re-tests before resolution.
governingDocuments..github/workflows/self-test.yml: Required Self-Test path. Pushes and PRs invoke the Orchestrator's test-only critical Code cadence before the governed natural-language/change-impact request; workflow_dispatch passes explicit requests unchanged.
Report-only cadence trigger. It passes daily, twice-weekly, weekly, or monthly cadence windows to the Orchestrator and never chooses test files itself.
governingDocuments.governingDocuments/known-bugs/README.md: Known-bug governance policy, criticality order, persistence behavior, progress-update cadence, and mandatory re-test lifecycle.
governingDocuments.governingDocuments/known-bugs/KNOWN-BUGS: Governed severity-sorted known-bug ledger. Resolved or checked entries are invalid unless their latest recorded re-test passed.

sessionPolicy.recheckGoverningDocuments: Re-read every file listed in governingDocuments at the start of every session and again any time more than 10 minutes have passed since lastActionAt, even if it is the same agent continuing the same conversation.

syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.description: The CRUCIBLE TEST REQUEST synthetic commit-message transport exists only because the current ChatGPT/GitHub integration cannot directly create the required Orchestrator invocation. It is a workaround, not the intended architecture.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.replacementRequirement: Replace and remove this workaround as soon as a supported direct integration or direct connection exists that can pass the user's natural-language test request to the Orchestrator without manufacturing a repository commit.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.targetArchitecture: User test request -> supported direct integration/connection -> Orchestrator -> Orchestrator alone selects and runs tests -> results.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.standingOwnerAuthorization: The owner explicitly authorizes the governed agent to perform this specific replacement as soon as the supported direct integration/connection capability exists. No additional owner approval is required solely to replace and remove the synthetic test-request transport.
syntheticTestRequestCommitTransport.scopeBoundary: This standing authorization applies only to replacing the temporary test-request transport with a genuine direct integration/connection. It does not authorize unrelated repository changes or promotion to main/release.

testCadencePolicy.selectionAuthority: The Orchestrator alone selects categories, subcategories, test files, scope, and execution. Workflows may pass requests or cadence windows but may not select tests.
testCadencePolicy.explicitRequestRule: A specific owner test request is interpreted and run immediately by the Orchestrator; scheduled cadence never converts a specific request into a random category and never delays an explicitly requested category.
testCadencePolicy.codeCriticalityRule: Code is the critical baseline and its complete Code category is invoked by the Orchestrator on every push and pull request. That baseline is test-only so it does not duplicate the scheduled audit stack. It remains additive to the Orchestrator's request/change-impact decision.
testCadencePolicy.scheduledCumulativeRule: Scheduled cadence is cumulative: daily includes Code and Security; twice-weekly includes Code, Security, and Utility; weekly and monthly include all four categories.
testCadencePolicy.twiceWeeklySchedule: Utility cadence is triggered Tuesdays and Fridays by scheduled-diagnostics.yml; the workflow passes only the twice-weekly cadence window and the Orchestrator selects the tests.

activePlan.objective: Make the Orchestrator own differentiated test cadence by criticality while preserving immediate specific-request behavior and sole test-selection authority.
activePlan.currentPrompt: make the Orchestrator know certain things like code run every line, because its critical, other things like security even though its critical only need to be daily, things like maintenance  are weekly while utility are twice weekly

Keep scheduled diagnostics as cadence-window transport only; it never selects test files.

Verify corrected Self-Test and CodeQL after the follow-up development push.
